description: Rust transactional aggregate with observed local JetStream provider
qualification: normal local combined-source Linux node and ephemeral demo trust
observations: A disposable JetStream stream was qualified and the node reported its exact configured event profile. The Rust authoring capture pinned that profile and its companion-linked requirements; the maintained compiler and packager produced a component and the explicit demo signer produced its release.
The normal node admitted the signed release, applied narrowly scoped state and event policies, and accepted an authenticated update against an initially empty namespace.

The original command was committed with one effect; an authorized command lookup matched the original durable result, a fresh query returned count one, the effect reported provider acknowledgement, and the real stream contained one message.
The node was reaped after clean shutdown and reported physical retirement of its effect and state owners. The fixture removed its own broker, stream storage and TLS files.
limitations: This is one local successful Rust command and query using a disposable real broker. It does not prove rejection, stale conflicts, lost response, retries, crash boundaries, cancellation or full Rust acceptance.
The node is a normal binary built from a verified local combined-source snapshot containing unmerged work, not current development, an installed distribution or hosted CI.
The signer uses ephemeral local demo trust; production signing and release qualification are not established. A single broker message does not establish universal exactly-once delivery.
